examTitle: Geography of Ethiopia & the Horn (GeES 1011) - Mid-Exam (2016 E.C)
department: Department of Geography and Environmental Studies

questions.question: Expanding irrigation agriculture in its vast lowlands can help Ethiopia boost its food production in the future.
questions.explanation: Ethiopia's vast lowlands possess significant river basins and irrigable command areas suitable for large-scale agricultural transformation.

questions.question: There is no perfectly compact shaped nation in the world so far.
questions.explanation: A perfectly compact state would be an exact theoretical circle; no nation in the world possesses an ideally circular border.

questions.question: Most of the population in Ethiopian highlands pursue the pastoral way of life.
questions.explanation: The highland population predominantly practices sedentary mixed agriculture (crop-livestock cultivation), while pastoralism dominates the lowlands.

questions.question: Ethiopia has longer latitudinal extension than its longitudinal one.
questions.explanation: Ethiopia extends about 12 degrees north-south (3°N to 15°N) and 15 degrees east-west (33°E to 48°E), meaning its longitudinal extension is greater.

questions.question: The proportion of lowlands exceed highlands in Ethiopia.
questions.explanation: In Ethiopia, highlands (elevations above 1,000 meters) constitute about 56% of the country, exceeding the lowlands.

questions.question: The approach of studying mineral production in Africa is more of systematic.
questions.explanation: Studying a specific topic or commodity (such as mineral production) across a region follows the systematic (thematic) approach in geography.

questions.question: A substantial proportion of Ethiopia's population lives within the Rift Valley system today.
questions.explanation: A significant portion of the Ethiopian population resides within the Rift Valley lakes region, Hawassa, Adama, and surrounding urban centers.

questions.question: The Southeastern lowlands in Ethiopia have an immense potential for petroleum extraction.
questions.explanation: The Ogaden sedimentary basin in the southeastern lowlands holds substantial confirmed reserves of natural gas and hydrocarbon potential.

questions.question: The Chew Bahir region is the lowest most point region in Ethiopia.
questions.explanation: The lowest point in Ethiopia is the Danakil Depression (Kobar Sink) at approximately 125 meters below sea level, not Chew Bahir.

questions.question: Djibouti has smaller area and less compact than Ethiopia.
questions.explanation: While Djibouti has a much smaller area than Ethiopia, its boundary-circumference shape index shows it is not necessarily less compact than elongated shapes.

questions.question: If you stand on one side of the deep river valley gorges of Abay and observe all the exposed vertical cross-cutting layers of the earth profiles, which of the following layers is probably missing?
questions.explanation: The Paleozoic Era was predominantly a time of denudation and peneplanation in the Horn with minimal sedimentary deposition, creating an unconformity.

questions.question: Which mineral is largely dominated in the Afar Depression than elsewhere in Ethiopia?
questions.explanation: The Danakil Depression in the Afar region contains world-class evaporite deposits, predominantly potash and rock salt.

questions.question: Which of the following geomorphic processes truly explains the characteristics of exogenic processes?
options: Mostly result in building of structural features like plateaus
questions.explanation: Exogenic processes operate on the surface powered by solar energy and gravity, primarily causing weathering, erosion, and denudation.

questions.question: The principle of original horizontality states that:
options: Most rocks in the earth's crust are layered horizontally
Igneous rocks form essentially horizontal layers
Metamorphic gradients are essentially horizontal before deformation
Sediments are deposited as essentially horizontal layers
questions.explanation: Steno's law of original horizontality states that layers of sediment are originally deposited horizontally under the action of gravity.

questions.question: Fossils are most common in which rock types?
options: All of these commonly contain fossils
questions.explanation: Sedimentary rocks preserve organic remains because they form at low temperatures and pressures without melting or extreme recrystallization.

questions.question: Which era was dominated by the dinosaurs?
questions.explanation: The Mesozoic Era (Age of Reptiles) encompasses the Triassic, Jurassic, and Cretaceous periods dominated by dinosaurs.

questions.question: What is the Mesozoic supercontinent that consisted of all landmasses of the present continents?
questions.explanation: Pangaea was the supercontinent that assembled in the late Paleozoic and persisted into the early Mesozoic before rifting.

questions.question: Which of the following eras represents the longest time period in Earth's history?
questions.explanation: The Precambrian spans roughly 4 billion years, covering approximately 88% of geologic time.

questions.question: Which one of the following features is identified with the rift valley system within Ethiopia?
options: Hostile environment for all forms of life
questions.explanation: The rift floor features exceptional geothermal energy potential (e.g., Aluto Langano) and volcanic complexes, supporting various settlements and ecosystems.

questions.question: Which one of the following is a typical feature of lowlands in Ethiopia?
options: They are free from tropical diseases
They receive mild to high amounts of rainfall
They occupy most of the central parts of Ethiopia
questions.explanation: Lowlands in Ethiopia are sparsely populated due to arid climates, high temperatures, and endemic tropical diseases like malaria.

questions.question: Which of the following sub-divisions of the Western Highlands covers the largest area of the region?
questions.explanation: The North Central Massifs form the most contiguous and largest subdivision of the Western Highlands.

questions.question: The wettest part of the Ethiopian Rift Valley is the:
questions.explanation: The southern Main Ethiopian Rift (around Hawassa and the southern lake district) receives higher rainfall than the hyper-arid Afar or Chew Bahir basins.

questions.question: All of the following best describes major events that happened in the Mesozoic era EXCEPT:
options: Dinosaurs appeared and became extinct in this era
Epeirogenesis of the Horn of African landmass took place
The super continent begins to break up
questions.explanation: The major orogenic folding episodes occurred during the Precambrian, not the Mesozoic.

questions.question: Relatively, Ethiopia is situated:
questions.explanation: Ethiopia lies to the west of Djibouti (and Djibouti lies east of Ethiopia).

questions.question: Which of the following statements is true about the Mesozoic Sediments in Ethiopia?
options: The upper sandstone is the result of transgressions of the sea
The upper sandstone is older in the North West
Adigrat sand stone had occurred due to regression of the sea
The upper sandstone is thicker in the southwest direction
questions.explanation: Because the sea retreated towards the southeast, Upper Sandstone deposition started earlier (making it older) in the northwest.

questions.question: It is believed that the gigantic mountain ranges of the planet earth were reduced and the total topography became an undulating plain during the:
questions.explanation: During the Paleozoic Era, prolonged erosion reduced the high Precambrian mountains down to a peneplain.

questions.question: Which of the following statements best designates the process of uplifting of the Arabo-Ethiopian landmass and pouring of lava flood?
options: This huge uplift had occurred in the quaternary period of Cenozoic era
It had occurred after rift valley formation
It is continuation of Mesozoic era and reaches the maximum in tertiary period
The process began and completed in the tertiary period of Cenozoic era
questions.explanation: Uplift began toward the end of the Mesozoic (Cretaceous) and reached its maximum climax during the Tertiary period of the Cenozoic.

questions.question: Human beings evolved during which geologic era?
questions.explanation: Hominids and modern humans evolved during the Quaternary period of the Cenozoic Era.

questions.question: Which of the following Age Dating Techniques infers the absolute/actual age of a rock?
options: Counting the regular rates of decay for a given unstable element
Considering layers of rocks in a cliff or hillside
Identifying the type of fossil contained in the rock system
Considering the order of depositional materials in a given area
questions.explanation: Radiometric dating measures the radioactive decay rates (half-life) of unstable isotopes to determine absolute chronological age.

questions.question: Which of the following geologic activities and processes of the Cenozoic era took place first?
options: Volcanism in south of Lake Tana regions
Red Sea and the Gulf of Aden were connected
Trap series lava covers the floor of the uplifted landmass
questions.explanation: Massive flood basalt outpouring (the Trap Series) occurred during the early Tertiary prior to the major faulting and splitting of the Rift Valley.
